2.1.1. bool_expression_parser.code_api.parse¶

bool_expression_parser.code_api.parse(expression, vardict=None, prog=None, docstring=None, neg_sym='~', and_sym='&', or_sym='#', parse_all=False, new_variable_warning=True)¶

Parses the given expression (a string) and returns it as a CodeAPI PiExpression.

Throws ParseException if parsing fails.

It is possible to configure which symbols are used for different operators through the optional “X_sym” parameters. The default symbols are

  • “~” for negation
  • “&” for conjunction
  • “#” for disjunction
Parameters:
  • expression (str) – Expression to parse.
  • vardict (maybe({str: PiVariable})) –

    The supplied dictionary vardict is used to map string literals to variables. Strings “true” and “false” (ignoring casing) are mapped to constants TRUE and FALSE.

    If vardict is None, the vardict is constructed automatically from the PiProgram prog by mapping variable names to PiVariables.

  • prog (maybe(PiProgram)) – Program to populate vardict from, in case vardict is None.
  • parse_all (bool) – If parse_all is True, an exception is raised unless the entire string was consumed during parsing.
  • new_variable_warning (bool) – Issue a warning if new variables occur.
Returns:

PiExpression
